model.name: Recruitment / Hiring Process
model.purpose: Represent one governed recruitment process aggregate for a bounded hiring need or campaign, connecting an authorized requisition and frozen selection design to source-qualified candidate participation, accountable decisions, offers and closure.
model.scope_statement: Owns recruitment-process identity and lineage, mandatory process profile, authorized need and exact requisition and criterion bindings, posting and sourcing activity, process-scoped candidate-case links, stage design and occurrences, bounded screening, assessment, interview, verification, recommendation, decision, offer, response, closure, quality, fairness, lifecycle, interoperability, access and retention assertions. Organization, Unit, Position, Vacancy, Person, Candidate, Application, Qualification, Competency, Assessment Definition, Assessment Result, Interview, Evidence, Decision, Offer, Contract, Employment, Communication, Dataset, Artifact and Audit masters remain external.
in_scope: Process identity, profile, lineage, hiring need, requisition, authority, job analysis, competencies, qualifications, criteria and policy bindings
Posting, channels, sourcing, referrals, agencies, fees, candidate notices, application and candidate-case references, eligibility, accessibility, accommodations and protected-data controls

Screening, assessments, interviews, verification, ranking, recommendation, accountable selection, offers, responses, closure, complaints, quality, fairness, lifecycle, interoperability, retention and safe agents
out_of_scope: Independent organization, unit, position, vacancy, person, candidate, application, competency, qualification, assessment, interview, evidence, decision, offer, contract, employment, communication, dataset, artifact or audit master lifecycles
Inferring consent, qualification, eligibility, suitability, fairness, employment, legality or future performance from participation, one document, score, ratio, offer response or opaque model
Implementing an applicant-tracking system, job board, assessment platform, background-check service, HR information system, payroll system or universal employment and equality law

boundary_notes.neighbor: Position, Vacancy / Matching and Job Posting
boundary_notes.distinction: The position and vacancy define the opportunity and a posting is one published representation. The recruitment aggregate binds exact external revisions and coordinates a bounded hiring realization.
The process owns source-qualified participation and stage assertions. Person, candidate identity and application evidence retain independent ownership, rights and lifecycle.
The process binds exact definitions and records occurrences and bounded use. Instruments, observations, source evidence and result records retain their own identity, authority and correction history.
Scores and recommendations inform but do not become the accountable selection decision. An offer is a separately versioned proposal with its own issuer, terms, response and withdrawal history.
Offer acceptance and recruitment closure may trigger governed handoffs but do not create the contract, employment relation or onboarding lifecycle inside this model.

functions.name: Screen, assess and interview

functions.name: Verify, rank and recommend

boundaryDecision.rationale: WM-ACT-039 correctly identifies as aggregate: owns bounded recruitment-process identity and lineage, mandatory profile, lifecycle, orchestrates external entities (Position, Vacancy, Person, Candidate, Application, Assessment, Interview, Offer, Contract, Employment) while preserving their independent ownership and identity, maintains typed neighbor relations with documented source support, and enforces non-cascading composition semantics. The frozen registry classification 'standalone-mm' refers to the record plane, not the subject model entry kind; schema enum 'aggregate' is the most defensible alternative within the required kinds (entity, event, relationship, mixin, pattern, registry, classifier, aggregate).

decisions.concept: Entry kind (aggregate) and mandatory profile
decisions.rationale: The model owns recruitment-process identity, design release, lifecycle state transitions (draft, authorized, open, paused, closed, filled, cancelled, corrected, superseded, archived), requisition and criterion bindings, posting versions, sourcing campaign references, process-scoped candidate-case links, stage orchestration, evidence and decision records, offer versioning, and closure lineage. This satisfies aggregate semantics: a bounded root with identity, lineage, composition relations, and governed lifecycle. The mandatory profile pattern supports single-vacancy, pooled, internal, contingent, agency, public-sector, and cross-border variants with shared orchestration semantics.

decisions.concept: Ownership boundary and neighbor separation
decisions.rationale: The model explicitly separates process ownership from external master ownership: process owns orchestration, evidence binding, and lifecycle assertions; Position, Vacancy, Person, Candidate, Application, Competency, Assessment, Interview, Offer, Contract, Employment remain external masters with independent authority and correction history. Non-cascading deletion rules, purpose-bound access controls, and minimum-tombstone preservation prevent master-lifecycle transfer and maintain audit evidence. Five documented neighbor boundaries (Position/Vacancy, Person/Candidate, Assessment/Interview, Recommendation/Decision/Offer, Contract/Employment) with source refs (SRC-001, 004, 012) are sound.

decisions.concept: Source authority tier and accessibility
decisions.rationale: All 16 sources are first-party official materials for their respective standards, laws, frameworks or guidance. ISO 30405 is available here only through its public catalogue abstract, HR Open downloads require registration or terms acceptance, and ICO recruitment guidance remains draft after consultation closed. EEOC and OPM are United States and United States federal sources, while GDPR, EDPB guidance and the AI Act are European Union sources. WCAG coverage describes the digital accessibility baseline but does not prove implementation conformance. Accept for reviewable draft with source-access, regional and interoperability holds.

decisions.concept: Composition relations and external master mappings
decisions.rationale: The model correctly identifies five neighbor boundaries with source support but states 'No approved relation rows were supplied. The registry parent link to Vacancy / Matching and proposed organization, person, application, assessment, decision, offer, contract and employment relations remain candidate holds.' Composition-relation definitions (cardinality, optionality, temporal ordering, deletion cascade limits) must be approved and synchronized with external master models before schema merge. Proposed relations list: Organization, Unit, Position, Vacancy (as neighbors), Person, Candidate, Application, Competency, Qualification, Assessment, Interview, Evidence, Decision, Offer, Contract, Employment. Deferral gate: approved relation contract signatures.

decisions.concept: Privacy, sensitive data, and access control architecture
decisions.rationale: Default-deny access model with purpose-bound role views (hiring sponsor, manager, recruiter, assessor, decision-maker, rights steward, privacy steward, records steward). Sensitive-data compartments (health, accommodation, diversity, criminal, background) with restricted access, minimum disclosure, and deletion eligibility rules. Candidate rights routes (notice, opt-out, correction, deletion, appeal, redaction) are explicit. Redaction strategy includes candidate-identifier, contact-detail, compensation, health, diversity, assessment-content, interview-note, ranking, and rationale redaction policies. Audit logging requirement for actor, role, purpose, process scope, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected fields, and source revision without unnecessary protected-data copy.

decisions.concept: Adversarial check enforcement: inference rejection rules
decisions.rationale: The model explicitly rejects five inference collapses: (1) consent inferred from application, (2) qualification inferred from résumé or single document, (3) eligibility inferred from sourcing or discovery, (4) suitability inferred from one score, offer acceptance, or opaque model, (5) fairness inferred from 80-percent ratio or single metric without statistical and practical context. These rules are actionable, prevent category collapse, and block deterministic claims. Four-fifths rule cited as US enforcement heuristic, not universal proof of discrimination. Fairness indicators include conversion, stage volumes, candidate experience, adverse-impact measures with small-sample and limitations caveats.

decisions.concept: Interoperability and schema crosswalk (Schema.org, ESCO, HR Open)
decisions.rationale: Mappings are versioned (Schema.org current, ESCO v1.2.1, HR Open unversioned-requires-download) and loss-aware: document process, vacancy, posting, occupation, skill, candidate-case, application, stage, assessment, decision, offer mappings with declared omissions, semantic conflicts, access limits, and round-trip loss. Pinned source and target versions required. No full conformance or round-trip claim made. ICO guidance is draft. Round-trip testing must validate before interoperability claim; proposed relations held for standards review.

decisions.concept: Regional scope and jurisdiction-specific legal alignment
decisions.rationale: Model cites EEOC (US) and OPM (US federal) for selection procedures and hiring reform; GDPR, EDPB, and EU AI Act (European Union only); ICO (United Kingdom draft guidance). Private, public, internal, contingent, agency, volunteer, platform, and cross-border recruitment have different authority, equality, notice, screening, record and remedy rules per jurisdiction. Protected-class definitions, affirmative-action duties, accessibility (ADA vs. Equality Act 2010 vs. EU accessibility directives), criminal checks, work authorization, automated-decision safeguards, notice, appeal, and retention vary by region. Legal review required for each operational jurisdiction before promotion from reviewable-draft.

decisions.concept: Lifecycle and state-transition invariants
decisions.rationale: Lifecycle records typed events for draft, authorization, opening, pause, closure, fill, cancellation, correction, supersession and archive. Each transition records actor, authority, rationale, effective and recorded times, evidence and correction lineage. Reopened or repeat relations, predecessor and successor identity and version management preserve earlier released history. These are model rules and validation obligations, not a claim that every implementation already enforces immutability technically.

decisions.concept: Quality, fairness, and adverse-impact measurement framework
decisions.rationale: Process owns stage volume, time, conversion, source-qualified process quality, candidate-experience, fairness and adverse-impact observations at process scope. Group selection rates may be computed only where lawful, and the four-fifths rule is retained as a United States enforcement heuristic rather than a universal definition or proof of discrimination. Denominators, cohort definitions, statistical and practical context, sample-size limitations and improvement actions remain explicit. Downstream job performance is outside this aggregate and must not be inferred from process metrics.

publicationHolds: Codex single-provider fallback research: Claude Sonnet and Grok 4.6 each timed out on their one bounded 120-second attempt for WM-ACT-039. No external provider result was admitted. The source-grounded Codex fallback passed local schema validation and the required separate no-tools adversarial audit. The result remains reviewable-draft pending independent review or explicit owner authorization for canonical promotion, and this hold must remain visible.

Source access and version verification: official public pages were consulted for all 16 sources, but ISO 30405 was available only as a catalogue abstract, HR Open downloads require registration or terms acceptance, and ICO recruitment guidance remains draft. Re-fetch and pin every accepted source at canonical promotion. GDPR and the AI Act are final official EU regulations, not draft texts.

Composition relation definitions and the registry parent link to Vacancy / Matching remain candidate proposals because no approved relation rows were supplied. Synchronize typed identity, cardinality, ownership, temporal and no-cascade contracts with the external masters before claiming composition completeness; this does not block publication of the internally valid reviewable draft.

Jurisdiction-specific legal alignment review across United States, European Union, United Kingdom and other regional profiles is required before canonical promotion. Protected-class definitions, affirmative-action duties, accessibility, criminal checks, work authorization, automated-decision notice and appeal, retention, recruitment-fee exceptions and remedy routes vary by region. No universal hiring regime is claimed.

Interoperability schema-version pins and round-trip testing: Schema.org current, ESCO v1.2.1 (updated 2025-12-10), HR Open (unversioned, requires download and terms review). Semantic conflicts, access limits, and loss-aware mappings documented; pinned versions required before certification. ICO guidance remains draft.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Detailed recruitment-profile variant invariants per form class: single-vacancy, pooled/evergreen, internal mobility, contingent, agency, public-sector, cross-border. Mandatory profile addresses shared orchestration but variants require distinct closed-world assumptions, approval authority, retention, remedy, and fairness-metric constraints per form.

Full ISO 30405:2023 normative text retrieval and normative conformance validation; HR Open schema structure, versioning discipline, and round-trip cardinality validation; ICO recruitment guidance promotion from draft to final with UK equality and data-protection specifics.

Independent occupational psychology, assessment-science, and test-validity review: criterion development methods, job-relevance documentation, predictive-validity evidence, differential-prediction analysis, adverse-impact indicators, alternative-assessment recommendations per role and jurisdiction.

Candidate-experience audit and WCAG 2.2 accessibility conformance testing: posting language and simplicity, application-process friction, assessment-alternative provision, interview accommodation, feedback timing, rejection-reason disclosure, appeal-route clarity, communication accessibility (audio/video/text/plain-language variants).
Independent external-provider review (Claude, Grok, or equivalent) after publication hold expires or owner reauthorizes. Single-provider artifact is time-bounded reviewable-draft.

model.name: Position
model.purpose: Model the position as a durable, addressable organizational construct that exists independently of any occupant: the work assigned by competent authority, classified, placed, funded, requirement-bearing and lifecycle-governed, so agents can create, inspect, classify, staff and retire positions without conflating them with people, jobs or contracts.
model.scope_statement: In scope is everything that is true of a position while it is vacant. A position is the bundle of duties and responsibilities assigned by competent authority (5 CFR 511.101) and modelled as org:Post, which W3C defines as a position existing independently of the person or persons filling it. The model owns identity, titling, duty content, occupational and grade classification, structural placement and reporting, location and work arrangement, capacity (FTE/headcount) and funding, requirements and essential functions, delegated and prescribed authority, risk/screening designations, working conditions, lifecycle and effective-dated change, governance and evidence, and outbound interoperability. It does not own the person, the occupancy relationship, the employment contract, the recruiting workflow, or the taxonomies it aligns to.
in_scope: Position identity, keys, official and working titles, and language-tagged alternative labels
Assigned duties, responsibilities and essential functions attributed to the position rather than to an incumbent
Occupational classification, job/class membership, grade or level and job-evaluation outcome
Placement in an organizational unit, cost centre, reporting and supervisory structure
Work location, work arrangement and schedule attributes attached to the seat
Capacity and occupancy control: FTE, headcount, single vs pooled, overlap tolerance, vacancy state
Budget, funding source and the pay range or grade ladder framing the seat
Qualification, competency, credential, screening, clearance and approval requirements
Delegated decision rights and externally prescribed regulatory responsibilities allocated to the seat
Lifecycle states, effective-dated versioning, classification authority, certification, appeal and retention
out_of_scope: The natural person, worker or agent identity that may occupy the position
The occupancy relationship itself (appointment, assignment, tenure, occupancy dates) — owned by WM-ORG-016
The organizational unit as an entity, its charter and its own hierarchy — owned by WM-ORG-002
Team formation and team-level goals — owned by WM-ORG-003
Employment contract terms, payroll processing, absence and time records
Recruiting workflow: requisition approval chain, candidate pipeline, interview and selection records
The occupation, skill and competency taxonomies themselves (ISCO-08, ESCO, O*NET-SOC, NICE) — referenced, not owned
Individual performance appraisal, development plans and remuneration paid to an incumbent
Compensation plan and pay-structure master data (grade ladders and steps are referenced by key)

boundary_notes.distinction: The position persists while vacant; the assignment exists only while an agent occupies it. W3C separates org:Post (independent of holder) from org:Membership, which exists only when an agent occupies a role. Occupancy dates, tenure and incumbent-specific terms belong to the assignment, not the position.

A unit is a collection of people and functions with its own recognition inside a larger organization; a position is a single seat that is contained in exactly one unit at a time via org:postIn / org:hasPost. Unit charter, mandate and unit hierarchy stay with WM-ORG-002.

A position is an instance; a class is 'all positions which are sufficiently similar as to kind of work, level of difficulty and responsibility, and qualification requirements' (5 CFR 511.101), and an occupation is 'a set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterised by a high degree of similarity' (ISCO-08). Classifier definitions, code lists and hierarchies are external registries; the position holds only the coded reference and the evaluation evidence.

A vacancy notice is a published recruiting artifact with its own validity window, datePosted, validThrough and application channel; it is a projection referencing zero, one or many positions. HR Open keeps PositionOpening in the recruiting domain and organizational structure with incumbents in OrganizationChart.

W3C org:Role denotes the abstract role and requires a Membership instance to link a person, whereas org:Post is a concrete organizational seat. Role vocabularies (NICE work roles, ESCO occupations) are alignments, not the position itself.

Pay range, grade ladder and budget frame the seat; actual remuneration, contractual clauses and payroll results attach to the occupant's employment relation. EU pay-transparency duties bind the employer's disclosure at recruitment and reporting, not the position record's internal semantics.

functions.name: Establish position
functions.description: Create a new seat by recording the duties assigned by competent authority, mint its identifier and place it in a unit.
inputs: holding unit and business unit references
outputs: position master record in proposed status
preconditions: competent authority has assigned the duties
holding unit exists and is active
identifier namespace is declared by the owner package
effects: a new position identity exists and is addressable
hiring status is set to proposed
an establishment decision is appended to the change history

functions.name: Classify position
functions.description: Analyse the assigned duties and place the position in an internal class and one or more external occupational codes.
inputs: classification plan or job catalogue reference
outputs: occupation code assertions with scheme and version
preconditions: a current position description exists
the classifier holds classification authority
scheme versions are pinned
effects: position becomes comparable across statistics and systems
classification effective date is recorded separately from the decision instant

functions.name: Evaluate and level position
functions.description: Apply objective, gender-neutral evaluation criteria to assign a grade and allocate the position to a category of workers.
preconditions: evaluation scheme is documented as objective and gender-neutral
skills, effort, responsibility and working conditions are all assessable
effects: position is levelled and comparable for equal-value analysis
pay range derivation basis becomes available

functions.name: Set capacity and funding
functions.description: Authorize FTE, headcount, position type and overlap tolerance, and bind the seat to a budget and funding source.
inputs: budget amount, currency and fiscal period
preconditions: budget authority approval is present
capacity values are internally consistent
effects: occupancy validation gains an enforceable ceiling
establishment and budget reporting can include the seat

functions.name: Specify requirements and essential functions
functions.description: Record essential and marginal functions, competencies, credentials and experience required of any holder, using versioned catalogue references.
preconditions: duties are decomposed at task granularity
catalogue versions are pinned
analysis is authored before advertising or interviewing
effects: requirements become auditable evidence for selection and accommodation decisions

functions.name: Allocate authority and prescribed responsibilities
functions.description: Confer decision rights on the seat and allocate any regulator-prescribed responsibilities to it without leaving gaps.
preconditions: the position is sufficiently senior for the responsibilities
gap analysis across the firm has been performed
effects: accountability is attributable to a designated seat independent of turnover
vacancy behaviour for each delegation is defined

functions.name: Designate risk and screening requirements
functions.description: Determine the clearance, vetting, regulatory approval and access requirements that attach to the seat before recruitment starts.
inputs: access entitlements implied by the duties
outputs: position risk and screening designation record
preconditions: duties and access entitlements are known
the applicable regime is identified for the seat's jurisdiction
effects: recruitment and provisioning can enforce prerequisites
lapse handling rules become executable

functions.name: Reconcile occupancy and vacancy
functions.description: Compute consumed and open capacity from assignment records and validate incoming occupancy against the authorization.
inputs: current assignment references and consumed capacity
preconditions: assignment records are readable from the occupancy model
capacity authorization is current at the as-of date
effects: vacancy is derived rather than asserted
capacity breaches are warned or blocked per the overlap flag

functions.name: Amend or reclassify position
functions.description: Apply an effective-dated change to duties, placement, capacity or classification, distinguishing correction from substantive change.
outputs: re-issued description or evaluation where triggered
preconditions: authorizing party holds the relevant authority
effective date does not silently overwrite prior versions
effects: prior versions remain queryable as of their effective windows
dependent artifacts are flagged for review

functions.name: Certify description and process appeals
functions.description: Certify the accuracy of the position description and administer challenges to its classification, applying decision effective dates.
outputs: corrected classification with its effective date
preconditions: the description states the duties actually assigned
the appellant and the matter are within scope of appeal
effects: the record becomes evidentiary
corrected classifications take effect on their own governed date

functions.name: Publish position projection
functions.description: Generate an outbound projection of the position for a named recipient profile, applying suppression rules and disclosure duties.
outputs: pay range disclosure record where required
preconditions: position is in an approved status for staffing projections
required pay-range disclosure has been determined for the jurisdiction
effects: downstream systems and the public receive a governed subset
disclosure evidence is retained

functions.name: Freeze, abolish or dispose position
functions.description: Move the seat to frozen or abolished status and, at the end of retention, apply the governed disposition action to its records.
preconditions: occupancy preconditions are satisfied or explicitly overridden
no preservation hold is active before disposition
effects: the seat stops consuming establishment and budget
history is preserved until retention expiry, then disposed with an auditable record

functions.name: Authorize fill or freeze
functions.description: Permit or withhold recruitment against a vacant Position, producing a fill-authorization that a JobPosting or requisition may reference.
preconditions: Position is established and not abolished.
Classification and PD are adequate if the local regime requires them before advertisement.
effects: A JobPosting may be linked as an advertisement of this vacancy; the posting is not the Position.
Freeze withholds fill without abolishing the slot.

composition.target: WM-ORG-002 Organizational unit
composition.purpose: Every position is contained in exactly one organizational unit at a given effective date, matching org:postIn / org:hasPost and the mandatory department reference in production position records.

composition.target: WM-ORG-003 Team
composition.purpose: Teams are composed through positions and their assignments; positions remain reusable across team formations and are referenced, not owned, by the team model.

composition.target: WM-ORG-016 Assignment / occupancy
composition.purpose: A position is occupied through a scoped assignment; occupancy, tenure and incumbent-specific terms live there, mirroring the org:Post versus org:Membership separation, and supply the consumed capacity used to derive vacancy.

composition.target: Job / class / occupation classifier model (sibling; registry entry not yet identified)
composition.purpose: The class grouping similar positions and the occupational category are external classifier concepts; the position holds only coded references, not the class definitions or hierarchies.

composition.target: Person / worker identity model (sibling; registry entry not yet identified)
composition.purpose: Incumbents are referenced only indirectly through assignments so that the position record carries no personal data of its own.

composition.target: ISCO-08 (International Standard Classification of Occupations)
composition.purpose: Alignment target for occupational coding and for the job-versus-occupation distinction; mapping strength and version are recorded and conformance is not claimed without assessment evidence.

composition.target: ESCO occupations pillar
composition.purpose: Alignment target for multilingual labels, scope notes, regulatory aspects and essential or optional skills at ISCO level 5 and below.

composition.target: O*NET Content Model
composition.purpose: Alignment target for duty decomposition into work activities, for requirement typing and for environmental work-context descriptors.

composition.target: W3C Organization Ontology (org:Post)
composition.purpose: Ontological alignment for publishing positions as graph nodes with postIn, heldBy and reportsTo edges, and for the vacancy-independent semantics of a post.

composition.target: HR Open Standards 4.5 (OrganizationChart, PositionOpening, PositionCompetencyModel, HRMasterData)
composition.purpose: Exchange alignment for organizational structure, recruiting projections, competency models and provisioning payloads.

composition.target: schema.org JobPosting
composition.purpose: Publication alignment for the advertisement projection only; the posting is a time-bounded document about the position, not the position itself.

composition.target: NICE Workforce Framework work roles (NIST SP 800-181 Rev.1)
composition.purpose: Alignment for composing Task, Knowledge and Skill statements into reusable requirement sets that organizations map onto positions.

composition.target: Effective-dated versioning and provenance mixin
composition.purpose: Supplies the bitemporal pattern separating business effective windows from RFC 3339 record and observation instants, reused by every attribute group in this model.

composition.target: Regulated-firm accountability extension (SM&CR-style designated functions)
composition.purpose: Adds prescribed responsibility allocation, statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps for positions in regulated firms without imposing them on all adopters.

composition.target: Statutory position-classification extension (General Schedule style)
composition.purpose: Adds statutory class, grade, official position description certification, classification appeal and effective-date rules for public-sector adopters bound by such a plan.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one owner package that is master for position identity, declare the master system of record, and state whether position codes are unique globally or only within a business unit.

The owner package must publish who holds establishment authority, who holds classification authority and which approvals gate the proposed-to-approved transition, since the definition of a position depends on assignment by competent authority.
The owner package must register every external scheme it maps to, pin the scheme version in use, and maintain the crosswalk table with mapping strength and recorded conflicts.
The owner package must declare the retention and disposition schedule for position records and artifacts, and the personal-data boundary that keeps incumbent data in the assignment model.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per Dimension and per master system, for example vr:wm-org-004/{dimension}/{master-system}/position/{position-key}. Publish a resolvable IRI per position when the organization graph is exposed, typed as org:Post. Never encode title, grade, unit or date into the identifier, because all four are effective-dated and mutable; codes may appear in a separate human-facing position code field whose uniqueness scope is declared.
registry_links: vr.wm-org-004 (this entry; nav path NAV.SOC.ORG.POS)
planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv for CONTAINS from WM-ORG-002, COMPOSE from WM-ORG-003 and COMPOSE to WM-ORG-016
External registries referenced by pinned version: ISCO-08, ESCO occupations, O*NET-SOC, NICE work roles, HR Open Standards 4.5

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is a format-neutral record; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are encodings that must round-trip the same canonical content.
Every coded value is stored as a scheme, version and code triple; a bare label is never canonical and never sufficient for a classification assertion.
Every label carries a language tag; the official title is distinguished from working and alternative labels by an explicit label role.
All instants are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; business effective dates may be full-date values and are held in fields distinct from record instants.
Collections are ordered deterministically by a stable key so that content hashes are reproducible across systems.
patch_rules: Changes to duty content, classification, grade, capacity, funding or authority create a new effective-dated version; in-place mutation of a closed version is prohibited.
Every patch declares its effective date, its change type as correction or substantive change, a governed reason code and the authorizing party.
Corrections restate what the record should always have said and must preserve the erroneous version with a superseding marker; substantive changes open a new business validity window.
Deletion of history is prohibited; a position is ended by closing its effective window and recording an abolition decision, and records leave only through governed disposition at retention expiry.
A patch that changes classification must carry the classification action effective date separately from the decision instant, since the two are governed differently.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional attributes or new crosswalk entries is a minor change; changing identity semantics, uniqueness scope, capacity units or a pinned scheme version is breaking.
Consumers must tolerate unknown codes and unknown optional fields rather than rejecting the record.
Re-versioning an external scheme requires an explicit re-mapping decision with its own instant; silent code carry-over across scheme versions is prohibited.
Derived values such as vacancy state must never be treated as stable inputs by consumers; they are valid only for the as-of instant at which they were computed.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system position identifier assigned by the HRIS or position-control system of record.
Governed global identifier or resolvable IRI, such as the org:Post IRI published in the organization graph.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension only where no upstream authoritative identifier exists, recorded together with the reason no upstream key was available.
Never an identifier: official or working title, grade, unit, cost centre, incumbent name, or any date.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All instants use RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, per the Internet date/time profile of ISO 8601; -00:00 is used only for the unknown-local-offset case and is not equivalent to Z. Event time, business effective date and observation or ingestion instant are recorded in separate fields and never conflated.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named wm-org-004--{dimension}--{position-key}--{artifact-kind}--{effective-or-instant}--v{n}, lower-kebab-case throughout, with the instant in RFC 3339 basic-safe form so that lexical order equals chronological order. Version numbers increase monotonically and are never reused after disposition.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact records a content hash over its canonical serialization plus the identity of the certifying or authorizing party. Certified position descriptions, evaluation statements, statements of responsibilities and appeal decisions are immutable once certified; any change produces a new version that references the hash of the version it supersedes.

policies: Position records must remain occupant-free: no attribute of a position may identify a natural person, because a post exists independently of the person or persons filling it and occupancy belongs to the assignment model.

Single occupancy must never be assumed. Concurrency is governed explicitly by position type, headcount and the overlap-allowed flag, since both the ontology and production systems permit a post to be held by more than one holder.
A position may not be advertised or staffed until its classification, requirements, risk and screening designation and any pay-range disclosure duty have been determined and recorded.

External standards are alignments, not conformance claims; a conformance assertion requires named assessment evidence with a method and date, and unresolved disagreements between schemes are recorded rather than silently resolved.
Derived state such as vacancy is computed, timestamped and never persisted as an independent assertion that could diverge from its inputs.
Classification, grade, pay-range and risk-designation fields are governed reads: access is role-scoped and every read of pay or sensitivity data is logged.
A Position may be created, classified, frozen, published and abolished without an occupant.
Occupant personal data, actual salary and tenure live on assignment records; access and retention of those fields follow privacy law, not the PD schedule.
Public official Posts may publish label, organization, area and vacancy while withholding HR evaluation content.
Reclassification, abolishment and fill-freeze are privileged operations with named competent authorities and audit.

read: Read a position as of a business effective date, returning the version whose effective window contains that date together with its record instants.
Read the change history of a position, including superseded versions, change types and reason codes.
Read derived occupancy and open capacity for an as-of instant, with the assignment references that were consulted.
Read outbound projections filtered by payload profile and by the suppression rules applicable to the recipient class.
create: Create a position only through the establish function, with duties assigned by a named competent authority and a holding unit reference present.
Mint the identifier under the owner package namespace following the identity priority order and record the assignment instant.
Create derived artifacts such as evaluation statements, designations and certifications as new serial versions, never as edits.
update: Update only by appending a new effective-dated version carrying effective date, change type, reason code and authorizing party.
Update classification only through the classification authority, recording the classification action effective date separately from the decision instant.
Update capacity or funding only with the corresponding authorization artifact present.
Reject updates that would place personal data of an incumbent on the position record.
delete: Hard deletion of position records or their history is prohibited while any retention period or preservation hold applies.
End a position by closing its effective window and recording an abolition decision with its effective date; the identifier is retired and not reused.
Dispose records only at retention expiry, by the governed disposition action, with an auditable disposition record naming the approving role and the RFC 3339 instant.
Erasure requests concerning a person are satisfied in the assignment or worker model, not by deleting the position.

roles.name: Position owner (competent authority)
responsibilities: Assign and revise the duties and responsibilities that constitute the position
Authorize establishment, freeze, reinstatement and abolition decisions
Certify that the position description states the duties actually assigned

roles.name: Classification and evaluation authority
responsibilities: Place the position in a class and assign occupational codes with pinned scheme versions
Apply objective, gender-neutral evaluation criteria and record criterion ratings
Maintain consistency across comparable positions and administer redetermination after appeals

roles.name: Position control and budget steward
responsibilities: Authorize FTE, headcount, position type and overlap tolerance
Bind the seat to budget and funding source and manage funding lapse handling
Reconcile establishment counts, open capacity and budget reporting

roles.name: Model data steward
responsibilities: Own the identifier namespace, uniqueness scope and crosswalk tables
Enforce canonicalization, patch and retention rules and run validation suites
Maintain the evidence ledger, integrity hashes and conflict records

roles.name: Compliance and regulatory officer
responsibilities: Allocate prescribed responsibilities without gaps and maintain statements of responsibilities and the responsibilities map
Determine risk, screening, clearance and approval prerequisites for the seat
Determine jurisdictional pay-transparency and reporting duties and retain disclosure evidence

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Read positions as of a stated effective date and honour pinned scheme versions
Treat derived state as valid only for its as-of instant and tolerate unknown codes and optional fields
Never infer classification, exemption status or authority from a title alone

access.default_rule: Position structural data is internal to the organization by default and readable by authenticated organizational agents at bundle and layer scope; pay, evaluation, risk, screening and authority data are restricted to named roles, and no scope grants access to identifiable incumbent data, which is governed by the assignment model.
exceptions: Published vacancy projections are public for their publication window and expose only the fields permitted by the payload profile.
Pay range must be disclosed to applicants prior to employment where the jurisdiction requires it, overriding the default restriction on pay data for that audience and purpose.
Aggregate pay information by category of workers is disclosable to workers and to regulators under pay-transparency and reporting duties, in aggregate form only.
Statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps are disclosable to the relevant regulator on request, including superseded versions.
Risk, sensitivity and clearance designations are restricted to compliance, security and staffing roles and are excluded from public and general internal projections.
Preservation holds override retention-driven disposition and suspend deletion until the hold is lifted.
Public-office transparency for elected or gazette Posts.
Named audit or legal-hold access to historical PDs.
Emergency fill against a vacant essential Position under recorded authority.
Unnamed FHIR-style clinical slots may expose service and location without a person.
audit_requirements: Log every classification, evaluation, capacity, funding, authority and status decision with the actor identity, the decision instant in RFC 3339 and the separately recorded effective date.
Log every read of pay-range, evaluation-criterion, risk-designation and screening fields with the reader identity, purpose and instant.
Log every outbound projection with its payload profile, recipient class, suppression rules applied, content hash and generation instant.
Log overlap and capacity-validation outcomes, including warnings, blocks and any override with the overriding authority.
Log disposition actions and preservation holds with approving role and instant, and retain the log beyond the disposition of the records it describes.
Record who classified, certified, froze, authorized fill, abolished or hard-deleted a Position, with event time and ingestion time.
Record access to occupant-derived views and to sensitivity-coded Positions.
Retain audit independently of occupant PII deletion.

required_fields: Crosswalk and scheme version pin URL
read_order: AGENTS.md — resolve Name, Type, Model ID and Registry ID, then the Specification URL
Specification URL — scope, boundaries and the Bundle to Layer to Finding to Question structure before any read or write
Identity and namespace rules URL — identifier priority, uniqueness scope and timestamp rules before minting or matching any position
Storage type URL — how the format-neutral canonical record is projected into the storage in use, including effective-dated query semantics
Interface URL — read, create, update and delete operations, as-of query parameters and change-event emission
Processes URL — establishment, classification, evaluation, capacity, authority, designation, projection and disposition procedures with their required authorities
Access policy URL and Retention and disposition schedule URL — scopes, exceptions, audit duties and disposition actions before exporting or deleting anything

coverage.claim: Covers the position as an occupant-independent work-slot: identity and keys, official and working titles, assigned duty content and essential functions, occupational classification and grade evaluation, unit/cost-centre placement and post-to-post reporting, work location plus geographic area or constituency, capacity and derived vacancy, funding and pay framing, requirements, delegated and prescribed authority, risk and screening, working conditions, lifecycle and effective-dated change, governance, evidence, and interoperability including declared profile choice and abstract-role binding. Evidence is the fourteen base sources plus grok-sourced Popolo, HL7 FHIR and schema.org Occupation/EmployeeRole references. No claim of universal completeness: occupancy, employment contract, payroll, recruiting workflow and the referenced taxonomies are owned elsewhere, and retention periods, unpaid/honorary posts, military billets, academic lines and most non-US civil-service regimes remain declared gaps.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier, scoped position code, published IRI and external identifier set, with an explicit rule that title, grade, unit and date are never identifiers. Grounded in org:Post and in production position-record keys where PositionCode is unique only within a business unit.

Proposed, approved, frozen, active, inactive and abolished states with transition authorities, occupancy preconditions and a reinstatement-versus-new-identity decision. Hiring status and activity status are modelled as independent, following observed production semantics.

Containment in a unit (org:postIn), post-to-post reporting (org:reportsTo), delegate positions, occupancy links to assignments (org:heldBy), equal-value peer groups and team references. Reporting is deliberately modelled post-to-post so it survives turnover.

Bitemporal discipline throughout: effective windows for business validity, RFC 3339 instants with explicit offsets for record and observation time, separate classification-action effective dates, publication windows, vacancy-since instants and metric as-of dates.

Per-assertion source references with observation or ingestion instants, an append-only evidence ledger, description-precedence evidence relative to advertising, and content hashes over canonical serializations.

Distinguishes assigning competent authority, classification authority, holding unit, business unit, legal entity, cost centre and funding source, and requires the adopting Dimension to name one owner package and master system.

Capacity and overlap validation, gap analysis for prescribed responsibilities, gender-neutrality checks on titles and evaluation systems, description certification, consistency review across comparable positions and named validation rules with severity and execution instants.

Default internal-only rule with role-scoped restriction of pay, evaluation, risk and authority data across all four scopes, plus named exceptions for applicant pay disclosure, aggregate reporting and regulator access, and read-logging duties for sensitive fields.

The structure, preservation holds, disposition actions and personal-data boundary are modelled, but no fetched primary source states retention periods for position records. Periods must be supplied per jurisdiction by the adopting Dimension; treat the retention finding as a required local determination, not as canonical guidance.

Version-pinned crosswalks to ISCO-08, ESCO, O*NET-SOC and NICE work roles with mapping strength and recorded conflicts, HR Open exchange objects, schema.org publication projection and org: graph publication, with conformance claims requiring assessment evidence.

Separates what kind of work (class and occupation) from how much (grade and evaluation), aligning the class definition, the ISCO job-versus-occupation distinction and the four objective evaluation criteria.

Internal delegated decision rights with limits and vacancy behaviour, plus externally prescribed responsibilities allocated to designated senior positions with seniority justification and gap analysis.
FTE, headcount, single versus pooled, overlap tolerance, budgeted flag, budget amount and currency, funding source including funded-by-existing-position, and derived open capacity.
Work location, arrangement type, seasonal windows and environmental context, with jurisdiction derived from location rather than asserted independently.

Metric definitions with explicit denominators, unit reconciliation between FTE, headcount and authorized establishment, aggregation by category of workers, and inclusion rules for frozen, proposed and unbudgeted seats.

Occupant-free rule for the position record, personal-data boundary markers, and routing of erasure requests to the worker or assignment model. Specific lawful-basis analysis is left to the adopting Dimension.

Position-derived access entitlements, clearance and screening levels with re-screening intervals, regulatory approval prerequisites and lapse handling, sourced from production position attributes and regulated-firm approval requirements.

known_omissions: ISO 30414 human capital reporting metrics could not be verified: iso.org returned HTTP 403, so no ISO metric definitions are cited and the measurement layer relies on production attributes and EU reporting duties instead.

Official US federal sources were unreachable (opm.gov connection resets; ecfr.gov, bls.gov and several .gov hosts returned 403 or redirected to an unblock gateway), so 5 CFR and 29 CFR text is cited from the Cornell LII reproduction rather than from eCFR, and OPM's position-designation guidance is not cited at all.

Works council, co-determination and collective consultation duties on position creation and change (for example German BetrVG-style participation rights) are not modelled; no primary source was verified.
Public-sector establishment ceilings, headcount control legislation and civil-service staffing plans beyond the General Schedule pattern are not covered.

Military billets, ranks, elected and appointed public offices, board directorships, honorary and volunteer positions are only partially served by this structure; their appointment and eligibility rules are not modelled.

Occupancy of positions by non-human agents (software agents, robots) is unresolved. The registry records a robotics factor of zero, and no fetched source addresses whether a post may be held by a non-person agent, although org:holds is defined over agents rather than persons.

Job architecture and career-path concepts (job families, career streams, progression ladders as structures rather than as grade ladders referenced by key) are deliberately left to the sibling job classifier model.
Contingent, agency and outsourced work arrangements are only referenced through HR Open's contingent staffing family; the boundary between a position and a supplier-provided service is not resolved.
Full ISO 30400:2022 term entries for job, role, position and FTE were not inspectable; only the standard’s existence, date and chapter map were confirmed.
HR Open Standards / HR-XML Position and PositionOpening schemas were not retrieved as open full text.
Military billet versus rank, NATO manning, and academic faculty-line or endowed-chair semantics lack primary sources in this run and are gaps rather than canonical layers.
National archives retention schedules (for example NARA GRS) and GDPR storage-limitation periods are not cited as specific durations.
Dual-incumbency overlap windows for succession, career-ladder intern positions, and union-exclusivity of a slot are widely practised but not given primary support here.
Corporate statutory officer roles (director, company secretary) as Positions versus board membership remain unresolved against a possible sibling governance model.
ESCO occupation pillar beyond its ISCO mapping was not fetched.
conflicts: Occupancy cardinality: W3C states a post may be held by one or more persons, while classical position control treats a SINGLE position as admitting one holder and only POOLED positions as admitting several. Resolved here by making concurrency explicit through position type, headcount and an overlap flag rather than by assuming either default.

Terminology: ISCO-08 defines a job as the tasks performed by one person for a single economic unit, which is close to what this model calls a position, while ESCO and O*NET reserve occupation for the class and production HCM systems use Job for the class and Position for the instance. The same word therefore denotes an instance in one standard and a class in another; every coded reference must carry its scheme.

Advertisement versus seat: schema.org JobPosting merges the advertisement with the described role and carries totalJobOpenings, whereas HR Open separates PositionOpening from OrganizationChart. This model treats the posting as a projection with its own validity window, and permits advertised openings to differ from authorized headcount.

Nature of a position: the regulatory definition treats a position as the work assigned to be performed by an employee, whereas production systems treat it as a container with capacity, budget and possibly many holders. The model keeps duty content as the definitional core and capacity as an authorization layer on top.

Title versus substance: titles are governed and publishable, but essential-function determinations and occupational classification rest on duties actually performed, so a title can never be used to infer legal status, exemption, seniority or classification.

W3C ORG models occupancy as org:holds/heldBy on Post and treats Post as a subclass of Organization so a group may hold it; Popolo forbids org:holds/heldBy, requires occupancy through Membership, and restricts holders to persons.

HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole is primarily a period-bounded practitioner-at-organization-and-location record (assignment-shaped) that can also represent an unnamed slot; it is not equivalent to a classified HR Position or to org:Post.

ISCO ‘job’ (tasks of one person) and ‘occupation’ (set of similar jobs) are not the same as a US ‘position’ (work assignable to an employee) or a civic ‘post’ (organization-specific slot). schema.org Occupation is the profession kind; EmployeeRole is occupancy-and-pay.
schema.org Role.roleName / numberedPosition includes sports playing-position, which must not be imported as WM-ORG-004.
US GS class/grade/title rules are jurisdiction-specific; using them as if they were global would be a false conformance claim.
regional_assumptions: Pay-range disclosure prior to employment, the salary-history prohibition, gender pay-gap reporting at 100+ employees and gender-neutral job evaluation guidance follow Directive (EU) 2023/970, whose transposition deadline was 7 June 2026; national implementations differ in thresholds and timing, and comparable US state and municipal pay-transparency laws are not modelled.

The essential-functions construct, its factor tests and the evidentiary weight of a written job description prepared before advertising are US ADA regulatory concepts; other jurisdictions impose different accommodation and documentation duties.

The position, class and grade definitions and the classification appeal and effective-date machinery are drawn from the US federal General Schedule plan and apply directly only to positions covered by it; they are offered as an extension, not as a universal requirement.
Allocation of prescribed responsibilities, statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps follow the UK FCA senior managers regime and apply only to firms within its scope.
ISCO-08 skill levels reference ISCED-97 education categories, so cross-national comparisons depend on the education mapping in force in each country.
Currency, working-time standards used to derive FTE, probation periods and seasonal patterns are jurisdiction-dependent and must be declared by the adopting Dimension.
US Title 5 and OPM PD practice are used as a high-resolution public-service profile, not as a world default.
Popolo geographic-area and abolished-constituency examples are civic/legislative and may be unused in private-sector HR.
Ex officio Cabinet membership is a Westminster illustration in ORG; the pattern is reusable but the example is regional.
FHIR unnamed-surgeon pattern is healthcare-specific.
ISCO skill-level to ISCED-97 mapping is an ILO statistical convention and is not a hiring rule.
adversarial_checks: Tested the assumption that one position equals one incumbent and rejected it: W3C explicitly allows a post held by one or more persons, and production records expose POOLED position types, headcount above one and an overlap-allowed flag. The model therefore treats capacity as data rather than as an invariant.

Tested whether a position record is universally required and rejected the assumption: many organizations run job-based configurations in which assignments attach to a job with no position record at all. The composition link to the assignment model is therefore required from the position side but the model does not assert that every assignment must reference a position.

Tested whether a title can carry semantics and rejected it: essential-function determination rests on fundamental duties and on evidence such as time spent and consequences of non-performance, and occupational classification rests on work performed, so no consumer may infer classification, exemption or authority from a title.

Tested whether vacancy is an attribute and rejected it: vacancy is derivable from authorized capacity minus capacity consumed by assignments owned by another model. Persisting it would create a second source of truth, so it is modelled as a computed value with an as-of instant and no artifact.

Tested whether a published job advertisement is the position and rejected it: postings carry their own datePosted, validThrough, application channel and openings count, may reference many positions or none, and are governed by disclosure duties that bind the recruitment event rather than the seat.

Tested whether classification decision time equals effective time and rejected it: the governing regulation places effective dates of classification actions in a separate subpart from the decisions themselves, so the model records decision instant and classification effective date as distinct fields.

Tested whether external standards can be claimed as conformance and rejected it: all external schemes are modelled as ALIGN links with pinned versions, mapping strength and recorded conflicts, and a conformance assertion requires named assessment evidence with a method and date.

Tested whether identity could be carried by a stable-looking business code and rejected it: position codes were found to be unique only within a business unit, so the code is retained as a scoped label while identity priority runs master-system identifier, then governed IRI, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID.
If a record cannot exist when vacant, it is an assignment or membership, not a Position.
If the only identifier is a person’s name, employee number or a start date, identity is wrongly sourced.
If CEO is modelled once globally rather than as CEO-at-organization, a Role has been stored as a Position.
If ISCO unit group is used as the Position id, an occupation has replaced the slot.
If a JobPosting is treated as the Position, a recruitment advertisement has replaced establishment.
If acting coverage rewrites official title or grade, occupancy has leaked into the slot.
If financial holdings, map coordinates or Quarterback are accepted as instances, the wrong sense of position has been admitted.
If org:holds is persisted under a Popolo profile, the declared interoperability profile is violated.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently classify WM-ORG-004 as an entity and both anchor it on the same test: the record must be able to exist while vacant. That test is decidable, is grounded in W3C ORG (org:Post exists independently of the person filling it) and in the regulatory definition of a position as work assigned by competent authority, and it cleanly separates the seat from occupancy (WM-ORG-016), from the unit (WM-ORG-002), from the abstract role, and from the recruitment advertisement. No split or reclassification is warranted; the base boundary is adopted as written, with grok's word-sense and FHIR disambiguations carried forward as boundary annotations rather than as new structure.

decisions.concept: Base provider selection
decisions.rationale: Claude offers a single decidable boundary test (everything true of a position while it is vacant), names the owning sibling model for each exclusion, carries roughly 1.4 times the base's own layer count in findings with four questions each, and declares one honest gap. Grok has more bundles and layers but nineteen findings across nineteen layers, so its topology is thinner per node despite the larger frame.

decisions.concept: Entry kind
decisions.rationale: Independent agreement between providers plus the vacant-existence test grounded in W3C ORG and the regulatory definition of assigned work; nothing in either pack suggests an event, service or relationship framing would fit better.

decisions.concept: Grok eight-bundle topology
decisions.disposition: rejected in favour of base topology
decisions.rationale: Grok's split of location, compensation and establishment into separate top-level bundles fragments concerns the base already integrates, and re-parenting the base's twenty-seven findings into nineteen thin layers would lose the base's explicit inline-only rationales without adding evidence.

decisions.concept: Abstract role binding
decisions.rationale: Materially absent from the base, evidence-backed on ORG, Popolo and schema.org, and consistent with the base's own statement that role vocabularies are alignments rather than the position itself.

decisions.concept: Geographic area and constituency
decisions.rationale: Distinct from duty station and work arrangement; Popolo ties post existence to area existence and schema.org scopes occupational description by region, and the base's omissions list already concedes elected and appointed offices are underserved.

decisions.concept: Interoperability profile declaration
decisions.rationale: The ORG-versus-Popolo disagreement about direct holds is genuine and source-backed; recording the profile in force per instance is the mechanism that keeps it a declared configuration rather than an unresolved contradiction.

decisions.concept: Fill authorization
decisions.rationale: Closes the only real hole in the base function set and marks the boundary handoff to the excluded recruiting domain; narrowed to fill so it does not duplicate the base freeze and abolish function.

decisions.concept: Grok class, series and grade finding
decisions.rationale: The base already separates occupational classification from grade and job evaluation across two findings with twelve questions and both a classification evaluation record and a job evaluation statement; grok adds no evidence the base lacks.

decisions.concept: Grok occupation code alignment finding
decisions.rationale: Covered by the base occupational-classification finding plus the version-pinned crosswalk finding, both of which already require scheme, version and mapping strength; the ISCO armed-forces-major-group nuance is deferred instead.

decisions.concept: Grok position remuneration band finding
decisions.rationale: The base pay-range-and-transparency finding already fixes the position band against occupant pay and adds disclosure and reporting duties; only the unpaid, nominal-pay and fee-basis case is genuinely new and it is too thin to stand as structure, so it is deferred.

decisions.concept: Grok hosting organization finding
decisions.rationale: The base unit-and-cost-centre finding covers holding unit, legal entity, business unit and cost centre with movement semantics; the residual ex officio and Post-as-Organization dual-typing questions are deferred rather than injected.

decisions.concept: Grok constraints-on-the-position finding
decisions.disposition: rejected as split across existing layers
decisions.rationale: Its three elements land separately in the base screening-and-clearance, retention-and-privacy and pay findings; injecting it whole would create overlapping ownership of sensitivity and privacy rules across two bundles.

decisions.concept: Vacancy as derived state
decisions.rationale: Both providers independently refuse to persist occupancy on the seat and both cite ORG and the assignment boundary; the base's no-artifact rationale is kept because a stored vacancy flag would create a second source of truth against WM-ORG-016.

decisions.concept: Retention dimension status
decisions.rationale: Grok marks retention covered while its own notes concede national schedules were not fetched; the base's gap marking is the accurate one and no fetched primary source in either pack states a retention period for position records.

decisions.concept: Source identifier collision
decisions.disposition: re-key all source ids on merge
decisions.rationale: SRC-002 denotes HR Open in the base and Popolo in grok, and several other identifiers collide across providers while pointing at different documents; the synthesizer must re-key rather than union by identifier or every accepted addition will carry the wrong citation.

decisions.concept: FHIR and word-sense disambiguation
decisions.disposition: carried as boundary annotation, not structure
decisions.rationale: Grok's align-not-equate treatment of PractitionerRole and its exclusion of financial, geospatial and sports senses of position are correct and useful, but they are boundary prose rather than findings; they are recorded as a publication hold on the boundary notes instead of being injected as nodes.

publicationHolds: Source verification is incomplete: every base URL and version pin must be re-resolved at publication time. In particular the base cites 5 CFR and 29 CFR from the Cornell LII reproduction because eCFR and opm.gov were unreachable in its run, while grok reached eCFR current as of 2026-08-20 and the OPM classification standards PDF; re-verify and dual-cite or swap to the official host before publishing.

Source identifiers collide across providers with different underlying documents (SRC-002 is HR Open in the base and Popolo in grok, among others). All sources must be re-keyed during merge and every accepted addition re-pointed, and the merged source list re-verified as live, before any draft is published.

ISO 30400:2022 must not be cited as defining position, job, role or FTE: grok's own note concedes the term text was not inspectable behind the paywall, so only the standard's existence, date and scope are supportable. The ISCO-08 citation must likewise resolve to an authoritative ILO or UNSD host rather than the third-party netlify mirror used by grok.

Retention and disposition periods remain a declared gap. No fetched primary source in either pack states a retention period for position records, descriptions or classification decisions; the structure may be published only as a required local determination, never as canonical guidance.

Multi-profile domain validation is outstanding. Evidence concentrates on US federal General Schedule classification, UK FCA prescribed responsibilities, EU pay transparency and a single HCM vendor API. Before publication the model must be exercised against at least a civic or legislative profile (Popolo post with constituency), a healthcare profile (FHIR PractitionerRole unnamed slot) and a non-US private-sector profile, and every regional assumption must be labelled a jurisdiction profile rather than a universal requirement.

Published boundary notes must carry grok's disambiguations verbatim in substance: HL7 FHIR PractitionerRole is aligned, not equated, to a classified position, and the financial, geospatial and sports senses of the word position are excluded, including schema.org's Quarterback example of a named position.
deferredResearch: Post-as-Organization dual typing and ex officio membership conferred by holding a post (W3C ORG and Popolo), unresolved against the WM-ORG-002 unit and WM-ORG-003 team boundaries and against corporate statutory officer roles versus board membership.

Unpaid, honorary, nominal-pay, fee-basis, piece-work and volunteer positions, and statutory exclusions from classification and pay statutes such as 5 U.S.C. section 5102(c); currently only reachable through grok's rejected remuneration finding.

Military billets versus rank as personal status (including ISCO Major Group 0 alignment), academic faculty lines and endowed chairs, and elected or appointed public office appointment and eligibility rules.
Works council, co-determination and collective consultation duties triggered by position creation, reclassification and abolition; no primary source was verified by either provider.
Occupancy of a position by a non-human agent, unresolved in both packs even though org:holds is defined over agents rather than persons.
National retention schedules (for example NARA GRS) and GDPR storage-limitation periods as concrete durations for position descriptions, classification files and occupant-linked records.

Unfetched standard texts that would strengthen weakly supported areas: HR Open Position and PositionOpening full schemas, the ESCO occupation pillar beyond its ISCO mapping, ISO 30414 human capital metrics, and ISO 30400 term entries.
Dual-incumbency overlap windows for succession, career-ladder or intern positions, job-share fractions and union exclusivity of a slot, all widely practised but without primary support in either run.
