bundles.name: Civil identity core
bundles.description: The registered identity itself: the anchor that other models reference, and the core attributes a registrar establishes and maintains about it.
bundles.rationale: UN guidance defines legal identity as basic characteristics conferred through registration; ISO/IEC 24760 separates the entity from the identity information held about it. The anchor plus its registered core attributes must therefore be one coherent, separately governed concern.

layers.name: Identity anchor and record identity
layers.description: What the person entity is, how it is uniquely referenced within a domain, and how multiple records claiming the same person are reconciled.

findings.name: Person identity anchor
findings.description: The natural person as a persistent entity distinct from any record, identifier, document or credential about them, carrying the reference identifier every other model points to.

findings.name: Duplicate detection, merge and split
findings.description: Several records may describe one person across systems; the model must express same-as links, merge, supersession and split without destroying history or silently unifying distinct people.

findings.name: Exceptional identity paths
findings.description: UN LIA explicitly covers persons whose birth was not registered and refugees whose proof of legal identity may be issued by the host State or an internationally mandated authority. Statelessness is a named UN LIA concern. National CRVS practice also includes foundlings, unknown parentage, incomplete dates, delayed registration and, in some jurisdictions, presumed death and later identity restoration. Those last national cases are recorded here as operating needs with incomplete global normative detail.

layers.name: Registered core attributes
layers.description: The attributes a civil registrar establishes and maintains: legal names over time, birth facts, and the administratively recorded sex or legally recognised gender.

findings.name: Legal name as a versioned structured fact
findings.description: Legal name is a time-bounded, structured, script-bearing fact with an ordering convention, not a fixed string attribute of the person.

findings.name: Registered birth facts
findings.description: Date, precision, place and, where recorded, time of birth as registered, plus multiple-birth order, distinguished from the place and date of registration.

findings.name: Sex and gender recording
findings.description: Administratively recorded sex, legal gender recognition and self-identified gender are three distinct values with different code lists, owners and disclosure rules.

bundles.name: Identifiers and evidence
bundles.description: Scheme-qualified identifiers assigned to the person, the documents and attestations that evidence identity, and the assurance produced by proofing.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 24760 separates identifier from identity; UN legal-identity guidance treats documents as proof of a registered identity rather than the identity itself; NIST separates the proofing outcome from the resulting credentials. These three must be modelled as evidence about the anchor, never as the anchor.

layers.name: Identifier schemes and correlation
layers.description: How identifiers are assigned under named schemes with authorities and validity, and how their correlation properties are governed.

findings.name: Scheme-qualified identifier assignment
findings.description: An identifier attaches to the person under a named scheme with an assigning authority, validity period, format rule and reuse policy, without becoming the person.

findings.name: Identifier correlation and pseudonymity
findings.description: Cross-domain identifiers make a person correlatable across contexts; the model must record correlatability class and any pairwise or sector-specific pseudonym derivation.

layers.name: Identity evidence and assurance
layers.description: Issued documents and electronic attestations that evidence identity, and the proofing process that produces an assurance level.

findings.name: Issued identity evidence
findings.description: Physical documents and electronic attestations evidence a registered identity and assert a subset of attributes; they never constitute the person and their revocation does not revoke the person.

findings.name: Identity proofing and assurance
findings.description: The recorded outcome of resolving, validating and verifying a claimed identity against evidence, expressed as an assurance level with an expiry and an optional biometric reference.

bundles.name: Legal standing
bundles.description: The person's status in law: civil status, nationality or statelessness, legal capacity and any representation or support arrangement.
bundles.rationale: UN vital-statistics guidance makes civil status a registered legal fact; legal identity and nationality are the basis for document issuance; the CRPD constrains how capacity and representation may be recorded. Each is a separately governed legal state, not a demographic attribute.

layers.name: Civil status
layers.description: The registered civil or marital status, its effective date, governing jurisdiction and causing act.

findings.name: Registered civil status
findings.description: One current registered civil status per person with an effective date and governing jurisdiction; history is carried by the acts that changed it, not by overwriting the value.

layers.name: Nationality and statelessness
layers.description: Nationalities held, their basis and dates, and the distinct determination of statelessness or undetermined nationality.

findings.name: Nationality holding
findings.description: Zero, one or several nationalities held by the person, each with a coding, acquisition basis, dates and conferring authority.

findings.name: Statelessness and undetermined nationality
findings.description: Determined statelessness, undetermined nationality and simply unrecorded nationality are three different states with different consequences for document issuance.

layers.name: Legal capacity and representation
layers.description: The person's legal capacity state and any arrangement by which another party supports or acts for them.

findings.name: Legal capacity state
findings.description: Capacity is a time-bounded, domain-scoped legal state established by a legal act, with equal recognition before the law as the default and restriction as the evidenced exception.

findings.name: Representation and support arrangement
findings.description: An arrangement by which a person or organization supports or acts for the person, distinguishing supported from substituted decision-making and recording the person's own will and preferences.

bundles.name: Life course
bundles.description: The person through time: anchors to registered life events, the separation of occurrence time from record time, vital status and the lifecycle of the identity record itself.
bundles.rationale: Civil registration is defined as continuous recording of vital events from birth to death, with occurrence and registration consistently distinguished; ISO/IEC 24760 frames identity as passing through lifecycle states. Time handling is therefore a first-class concern, not an implementation detail.

layers.name: Life event anchoring and time
layers.description: How registered life events attach to the person and how occurrence, registration and ingestion times are kept apart.

findings.name: Vital and registered life event anchor
findings.description: The person carries typed anchors to life events resolved in the vital-event model, together with the role the person played in each event.

findings.name: Occurrence time versus record time
findings.description: Every person fact carries a time of occurrence, a time of registration and a time of ingestion; conflating them corrupts history and prevents lawful correction.

layers.name: Vital status and record lifecycle
layers.description: Whether the person is living, deceased or presumed dead, and which lifecycle state the identity record itself occupies.

findings.name: Vital status and death registration
findings.description: Vital status is an evidenced state; registered death, judicially declared death and presumed death are distinct and must not be collapsed.

findings.name: Identity record lifecycle state
findings.description: The identity record moves through governed states such as established, active, suspended and archived; transitions carry an authority, a reason and a timestamp.

bundles.name: Personal sphere
bundles.description: Data the person declares and controls: contact points, declared residence pointer, self-declared attributes and communication preferences.
bundles.rationale: UN legislative guidance and data-protection law both separate what an authority registers from what the person supplies about themselves. Mixing the two destroys the ownership boundary and misrepresents assurance.

layers.name: Contact, presence and declarations
layers.description: Person-controlled reachability, residence pointer and self-declared attributes, each explicitly flagged as unwarranted by any registrar.

findings.name: Person-controlled contact point
findings.description: A channel through which the person can be reached, owned and revocable by the person, with a verification state and per-purpose usage limits.

findings.name: Declared residence pointer
findings.description: A typed pointer to an address resolved in the place model, distinguishing legal domicile, registered residence and self-declared mailing address from statistical usual residence.

findings.name: Self-declared attributes and preferences
findings.description: Values supplied solely by the person, including communication and accessibility preferences, carrying no registrar warranty and always distinguishable from verified values in any projection.

bundles.name: Personal data governance
bundles.description: Lawful basis and consent, subject-right execution, minimal disclosure, retention, erasure and disclosure audit over person data.
bundles.rationale: Person data is personal data by definition; UN legislative guidance requires confidentiality and access control over civil-registration records, and EU law defines subject rights, special categories and storage limitation. Governance is therefore inseparable from the model, not an optional overlay.

layers.name: Lawful basis and subject rights
layers.description: Why each processing purpose is permitted, how consent is scoped and withdrawn, and how subject-right requests are executed.

findings.name: Lawful basis and consent grant
findings.description: Each processing purpose is bound to a lawful basis; consent-based purposes carry a scoped, withdrawable grant, while statutory registration processing is not consent-dependent.

findings.name: Subject right execution
findings.description: How access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection requests are received, decided, executed and evidenced, including lawful refusal.

layers.name: Disclosure, retention and audit
layers.description: What is released to whom in what minimal form, how long data is kept, when it may be erased, and what is logged.

findings.name: Minimal disclosure projection
findings.description: Each relying party receives the narrowest projection satisfying its stated need, preferring a derived predicate over the underlying attribute, with special-category data excluded by default.

findings.name: Retention, erasure and disclosure audit
findings.description: Retention classes and periods, the tension between permanent vital records and erasure rights, the method by which deletion is demonstrated, and what every disclosure must log.

bundles.name: Quality and interoperability
bundles.description: Attribute accuracy and correction, and disciplined alignment to external vocabularies including script and transliteration handling.
bundles.rationale: Accuracy is a legal principle for personal data and a quality requirement for civil registration; alignment to external standards must be recorded as mapping rather than claimed as conformance, and name transliteration is a documented interoperability hazard in travel documents.

layers.name: Attribute quality and correction
layers.description: Provenance and freshness of each attribute, the correction pathway, and the quality indicators measured over the person population.

findings.name: Attribute accuracy and correction
findings.description: Every core attribute carries a source and last-verified time; corrections supersede rather than overwrite, and population-level quality is measured.

layers.name: External alignment and encoding
layers.description: Versioned mappings to external vocabularies and credential schemas, and script, encoding and transliteration handling for names.

findings.name: External schema alignment
findings.description: Alignments to external vocabularies are versioned, explicitly lossy where relevant, and are mappings until conformance evidence exists.

findings.name: Script, encoding and transliteration
findings.description: Names exist in native script, transliterated and machine-readable truncated forms; each form must be identified, rule-bound and reconcilable to the registered name.

model.name: Offer / Quote
model.purpose: Represent one governed, versioned pre-contract commercial proposal so agents can understand who proposes what, to whom, for which price and terms, during which validity, with what evidence and response state, without confusing the proposal with a product master, negotiation, order, contract or legal formation decision.
model.scope_statement: Owns proposal identity, version, declared offer, quotation, estimate or informational profile; issuer and addressed-recipient roles; external product, service, right and resource references; lines, lots, bundles, options, alternatives and dependencies; quantities, units and eligibility; prices, currencies, formulas, tiers, recurring and usage terms; taxes, allowances, charges and totals; delivery, payment, quality, warranty, return, service-level, assumption, exclusion, rights and confidentiality terms; issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, expiry and knowledge times; attributable withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer and acceptance references; amendments, source, approval, quality, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Party, subject, catalogue, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response-event and legal-determination masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Proposal identity, versions, profiles, parties by reference, offered subjects, lines, lots, bundles, quantities, eligibility, pricing, taxes, totals and commercial terms
Fulfilment conditions, validity, lifecycle, response references, amendments, evidence, provenance, validation, access, retention and interoperable projections
out_of_scope: Owning Party, Product, Service, Right, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Shipment, Performance, Response Event, Legal Decision or Records masters
Treating a quotation, estimate, acknowledgement, click, conduct or technical status as universal proof of legal offer, acceptance, formation or enforceability
Autonomous pricing approval, tax or legal determination, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or physical records disposition

boundary_notes.distinction: The unfrozen object parent may supply generic object context but grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.

boundary_notes.neighbor: RFQ, negotiation, tender, order and contract
boundary_notes.distinction: A request asks for a proposal, negotiation exchanges positions, a tender follows procurement rules, an order requests performance and a contract records obligations. The proposal references but does not absorb them.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party, product, service, catalogue and price list
boundary_notes.distinction: These masters supply identities and source terms; the proposal owns only version-specific commercial assertions and references.
The proposal records attributable evidence and observed state but does not decide whether acceptance was effective or a contract formed under governing law.

boundary_notes.neighbor: UBL, schema.org, GS1, ODRL, PROV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI
boundary_notes.distinction: Each representation has different semantics and coverage; mappings are version-pinned and loss-declaring.

functions.name: Register an offer or quotation
functions.description: Governed operation to register an offer or quotation without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
preconditions: namespace, identity, issuer authority and profile checks pass
effects: a draft proposal exists without legal-effect inference

functions.name: Classify profile and jurisdiction
functions.description: Governed operation to classify profile and jurisdiction without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: qualified offer, quotation, estimate or informational classification
preconditions: classification criteria, jurisdiction, governing rules and uncertainty are explicit
effects: classification remains revisable and does not determine enforceability

functions.name: Compose subject lines and dependencies
functions.description: Governed operation to compose subject lines and dependencies without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: external product, service or right references
outputs: versioned lines, lots, bundles, options and dependencies
preconditions: subject masters resolve and cardinality, unit, option and dependency checks pass
effects: external subject lifecycles remain authoritative

functions.name: Calculate and bind pricing
functions.description: Governed operation to calculate and bind pricing without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: currency, quantity, tax, allowance and charge rules
preconditions: formula versions, units, currencies, rounding, tax jurisdiction and approval policy pass
effects: calculation produces evidence and never silently approves or mutates an issued price

functions.name: Bind commercial and fulfilment terms
functions.description: Governed operation to bind commercial and fulfilment terms without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: delivery, payment, warranty, service-level and rights terms
preconditions: term sources, dependencies, responsibility, jurisdiction and exceptions are explicit
effects: contract, order and fulfilment remain external

functions.name: Review, approve and issue a version
functions.description: Governed operation to review, approve and issue a version without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: immutable issued version and communication instructions
preconditions: pricing, tax, legal, commercial, access and approval checks pass
effects: the model records but does not autonomously sign, dispatch or publish

functions.name: Record communication and response events
functions.description: Governed operation to record communication and response events without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
inputs: attributable sent, received, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer or acceptance evidence
outputs: immutable event references and observed lifecycle assertions
preconditions: actor, authority, channel, receipt semantics, time, source and uncertainty are explicit
effects: no event or status automatically determines contract formation

functions.name: Validate an offer or quotation
functions.description: Governed operation to validate an offer or quotation without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
preconditions: identity, totals, taxes, dates, eligibility, authority, lifecycle and projection checks execute
effects: errors are reported without autonomous legal or commercial action

functions.name: Amend, correct or supersede
functions.description: Governed operation to amend, correct or supersede without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: successor version, comparison and communication requirements
preconditions: reason, affected lines and terms, prior responses, validity, authority and retention checks pass
effects: prior issued versions remain resolvable

functions.name: Query, project, retain and audit
functions.description: Governed operation to query, project, retain and audit without autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, contract formation, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.
outputs: filtered view, loss-declaring projection, retention result or audit event
preconditions: purpose, authority, privacy, mapping, digest, lifecycle and legal-hold checks pass
effects: representations never replace the canonical proposal and disposition stays external

composition.purpose: Project version-pinned legal, commerce, discovery, policy, provenance, quality, time, validation and API views with declared information loss.

Authoritative Party, Product, Service, Catalogue, Price List, RFQ, Negotiation, Tender, Contract, Order, Invoice, Payment, Fulfilment, Event and Records registries
Approved jurisdiction, tax, currency, unit, pricing, eligibility, delivery, payment, rights, privacy, retention and interoperability profiles

https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative proposal identifier, issuer namespace and version head, never by title, recipient, issue date, total, filename or digest alone.
Keep offer or quote, party, product, service, catalogue, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response event and records independently identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare profile, jurisdiction, identity, party, subject, line, quantity, price, tax, term, lifecycle, access and interoperability effects.
Issued versions are immutable; changes create linked successors with reason, affected terms, response impact, compatibility, migration and approval.
Never silently change profile, issuer, recipient, subject, quantity, price, currency, tax, total, term, validity, authority, response or legal-effect qualifier.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when identity, version, profile, parties, subject, price, currency, taxes, terms, validity, authority, access and provenance survive.
Every projection pins specification or vocabulary version and declares loss in line, pricing, tax, term, response, lifecycle and authority semantics.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for proposal, version, line, price component, term, event reference or artifact, qualified by issuer namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable proposal or artifact IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, record kind, proposal and version IDs, profile, issuer, actor, distinct event and knowledge times, confidentiality marking and provenance.

policies: The proposal owns its commercial assertions and versions but not external parties, subjects, negotiations, requests, tenders, contracts, orders, invoices, payments, fulfilment, response events or legal determinations.
Offer, quotation, estimate and informational proposal are explicit profiles; labels and statuses alone never establish legal effect.
Issue, delivery, receipt, effectiveness, validity, response, expiry and formation determinations are separate assertions.
Agents cannot autonomously approve pricing, determine tax or legal effect, accept, sign, dispatch, publish, widen access or dispose records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve proposal head, versions, profile, parties, subjects, lines, pricing, taxes, totals, terms, validity, events, evidence, access and projection loss under the permitted view.
create: Bind identity, issuer, declared profile, purpose, recipient scope, jurisdiction, currency, source authority and initial lifecycle before commercial assertions are accepted.
update: Append successor lines, prices, taxes, terms, approvals, communications, responses, corrections and lifecycle assertions with reason, authority, expected revision, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply legal hold, commercial-record, consumer, tax, privacy and adopting-Dimension retention policy; withdraw or tombstone only the catalogue view without cascading to external masters, and let authoritative systems execute physical disposition.

audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, proposal and version, operation, authority, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected lines or terms, source revision and outcome without duplicating restricted commercial data.

The WM-OBJ-003 parent signal has no frozen approved relation and grants no cascade authority.
Public procurement, securities, insurance, healthcare, utilities, travel, telecom, software subscription, construction and other sector profiles need separate rules.
National contract, tax, consumer, electronic-signature, records and privacy rules require jurisdiction profiles and authorized legal review.
Schema.org is a discovery vocabulary and does not establish legal effect or full transactional conformance.
conflicts: Offer, quote, estimate, proposal, invitation, RFQ, tender, counter-offer, order and contract are related but not interchangeable.

regional_assumptions: Offer formation, revocability, receipt, acceptance, tax, required disclosure, signature and retention depend on governing law, jurisdiction, party type and channel.

Reject autonomous pricing approval, tax determination, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening or records disposition.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The root is a versioned pre-contract commercial proposal aggregate with explicit legal-offer, quotation, estimate and informational profiles. Parties, products, services, catalogues, RFQs, negotiations, tenders, contracts, orders, invoices, payments, fulfilment, response events, legal determinations and records remain external masters.

decisions.concept: Offer, quotation, estimate and informational proposal
decisions.rationale: The shared structure is useful, but declared intent, definiteness, governing rules and legal effect differ; no label alone determines an operative legal offer.

decisions.concept: WM-OBJ-003 parent signal
decisions.rationale: The registry parent signal has no frozen canonical relation and grants no ownership, mutation or cascade authority.

decisions.concept: Proposal and neighboring commercial masters
decisions.rationale: Party, subject, catalogue, price list, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment and fulfilment identities and lifecycles remain external.

decisions.concept: Line, lot, bundle, option and dependency semantics
decisions.rationale: Composition preserves stable line and term identities plus alternative, substitution, minimum, partial and all-or-none rules rather than flattening them into text.

decisions.concept: Price and total semantics
decisions.rationale: List, unit, base, net, fixed, estimated, ranged, tiered, recurring, usage, tax, allowance, charge, subtotal and payable values stay distinct with currency, unit, quantity basis, formula, validity and provenance.

decisions.concept: Communication, response and contract formation
decisions.rationale: Sending, delivery, receipt, acknowledgement, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, counter-offer, acceptance evidence and formation determinations are separately attributable; no status automatically proves legal effect.

decisions.concept: Multiple temporal axes
decisions.rationale: Issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, delivery, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge times remain distinct and RFC 3339 timestamps require seconds and offset.

decisions.concept: Jurisdiction and consumer profile
decisions.rationale: CISG, UNIDROIT Principles and EU consumer requirements provide scoped reference profiles; national contract, tax, signature, privacy and records rules remain jurisdiction-qualified.

decisions.concept: Interoperability projections
decisions.rationale: UBL, schema.org, GS1, ODRL, PROV, DQV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI expose different subsets and never replace canonical proposal semantics.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts; assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-021 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external research result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-OBJ-003 is only a parent signal and no model relation is canonically approved for this aggregate.

Boundary hold: offer or quote, party, product, service, catalogue, price list, RFQ, negotiation, tender, contract, order, invoice, payment, fulfilment, response event, legal determination and records must retain separate identities.

Legal-effect hold: offer, quotation, estimate and informational profiles require explicit intent, governing rules and jurisdiction; no label, click, acknowledgement, conduct or status universally proves acceptance, formation or enforceability.

Pricing hold: every amount requires type, currency, unit or quantity basis, inclusion and exclusion, tax and charge treatment, formula or source, validity, rounding, approval and uncertainty qualifiers.

Temporal hold: issue, effective, receipt, validity, response, delivery, withdrawal, revocation, rejection, acceptance, expiry, observation, ingestion and knowledge time must never be silently collapsed; timestamps require seconds and timezone offset.
Authority hold: pricing approval, tax determination, legal classification, acceptance, signature, dispatch, publication, access widening and disposition require delegated accountable authority.
Jurisdiction hold: CISG, UNIDROIT Principles and EU consumer requirements are scoped profiles; national contract, tax, signature, privacy, records and sector rules require separate validation.
Interoperability hold: every UBL, schema.org, GS1, UNECE, ISO 4217, ODRL, PROV, DQV, JSON Schema and OpenAPI projection requires version pins, conformance evidence and information-loss declarations.

Privacy hold: recipient-specific prices, discounts, cost, margin, tax, negotiation, approval, contact, response and commercially sensitive data require purpose-bound access, minimization and retention controls.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
